On the noise that this test removes: JudgeSense (Bellibatlu, Raff and Zhang 2026, arXiv 2604.23478 v3) finds LLM judges disagree with themselves on identical prompts, most on graded tasks (Claude Haiku 4.5 coherence −0.206 against its own repeats), and Zhao, Esmaeili and Fard 2026 (arXiv 2604.16790) report two-run consistency of 70–90%; both predict noise of unknown sign, not a direction (`map/reads/remap-2026-11-05b-sg-b4.md`). What this bet adds: sg-b4's comparison with every cell graded in one run, Haiku twice, on the 5.5 models, which removes the cross-run confound its audit named. The engine's 16 sits below the papers' direction because the rule needs Haiku's mean to clear a bar its sg-b4 median (5.5) did not.

fields.prior_work: **Mixed; the nearest closing-line-only test predicts a small S of either sign.** Chen et al. 2026 (arXiv 2606.05976 v2, §4.4 and §4.5; Qwen2.5-72B, math): with a wrong claim left in the model's own assistant-turn <thought> block, changing only the trailing instruction moved explicit correction from 16.7% to between 0.0% and 33.3%, in both directions, while relabeling the claim's role reached 70.0%: a closing line moves the outcome less than structure does, and either way. JudgeSense (Bellibatlu, Raff and Zhang 2026, arXiv 2604.23478 v3): rewording a judge's instruction while keeping its question moves graded verdicts beyond repeat noise (pooled coherence −0.181), direction unstated. Khullar, Hopkins, Wang and Roger 2026 (arXiv 2603.04582; Claude 3.5 Haiku, Sonnet 4, Opus 4.1): explicit authorship statements move leniency within 0.5 of 10, i.e. up to 5 of 100, above both bars here, and they concern authorship, not a lead-in, so they bound S loosely and do not predict a miss. Grossmann and Kross 2014 (Psychological Science 25:1571): a third-person, distancing wording shrank a human self-other gap; an analogy only, since neither closing line refers to the self. Fox, Caspy and Reisler 1994 (found by the design review's search; abstract only): a cautionary instruction did not reduce human self-rating leniency, while changes to the rating scale and form did. What this bet adds over Chen: the first closing-line-only swap on a graded penalty for a planted overclaim, in a quoted User/Assistant transcript of the model's own conversation, on Claude 5.5 models, with both lines graded in one run. Why the engine's 14: the nearest test (Chen §4.4, §4.5) found closing-instruction changes small and of either sign beside structural changes, both Haiku and Opus must clear their bars, and Opus's 0.75 bar sits on a 1.5-point remainder over 30 studies.

fields.novelty_line: **Novelty:** partly new. Papers in print already show, in our direction, that a model goes easier on the same text in its own assistant turn than in a user turn (Khullar, Hopkins, Wang and Roger 2026, arXiv 2603.04582 v1, strongest on-policy; Tsui 2025, arXiv 2507.02778 v3), and they show the rival this test removes: LLM judges disagree with themselves across identical runs (Haldar and Hockenmaier 2025, Rating Roulette, arXiv 2510.27106: Krippendorff's alpha 0.265 to 0.563 over three runs on MT-Bench, three open-weight judges; Norman, Rivera and Hughes 2026, arXiv 2606.19544 v1: test-retest above 0.95 alongside position bias above 0.10), and human rating separates drift within a session from "scale instability" across sessions (Quellmalz 1980, CSE Report 136, abstract only). The nearest case of a self-favouring effect shrinking under a stricter comparison is Roytburg et al. 2026 (arXiv 2601.22548 v2: "only 51% of initial findings retain statistical significance" once a judge's votes for its own wrong answers are set against its votes for outcome-matched other models' wrong answers), which changes the baseline, not the run, and reports no repeated runs. A direct search found nothing in print that re-measures a quoted-copy leniency gap with every cell graded in one run, set against the same gap read across runs. Here Haiku 5.5's gap stays above zero but is 46% of its same-run blunting, under the 6.3 bar with an interval that cannot rule the bar out (its fall from sg-b4 is split between the two cells, neither shift distinguishable from zero, so run-to-run noise is neither shown nor ruled out as the cause), while Opus 5.5's holds at about its full size (+5.0, against sg-b4's +4.0). Search: WebSearch and arXiv abs/HTML, 2026-11-05: "LLM judge self-attribution bias same run versus cross run"; "LLM-as-a-judge test-retest reliability between sessions drift"; "monitor leniency own assistant turn versus quoted transcript in user message"; "self-preference bias replication measurement artifact"; "LLM evaluation nondeterminism score shift baseline from earlier run"; "batch effects high-throughput data"; "rater drift within-session versus between-session". By a fresh claude-opus-5-5 Novelty session (subagent).

fields.novelty_line: **Novelty:** partly new. That changing only the closing instruction of a self-review prompt moves the verdict a little, in either direction, and less than moving the text out of the model's own turn, is in print: Chen et al. 2026 (arXiv 2606.05976 v2, §4.4-4.5, Tables 4 and 7; Qwen2.5-72B math, n = 30) left a wrong claim in the model's own turn, swapped only the appended audit prompt, and saw explicit correction move from 16.7% to between 0.0% and 33.3%, against 70.0% with a system `<memory>` relabel. That rewording a judge's instruction while keeping its question moves graded verdicts beyond repeat noise, direction unreported, is in print for Claude judges (Bellibatlu, Raff and Zhang 2026, JudgeSense, arXiv 2604.23478 v3: coherence ΔJSS −0.206 for claude-haiku, −0.180 for claude-opus-4-7), and rewording a self-reflection prompt to verify rather than find mistakes cut false flips from 18.9% to 7.6% on Llama-3 8B (Liu et al. 2024, arXiv 2406.10400 v1). Not in print after a direct search: a swap of only "Now grade the conclusion above." for "Grade the conclusion." inside a quoted User/Assistant copy of the model's own conversation (the claim already out of its turn), scored as the penalty on a planted overclaim, on Claude 5.5 models with both lines graded in one run; ours fits Chen's picture of a small effect of either sign (Haiku +2.5 of 100 on a fragile mean, Opus +0.3), and no paper found separates such a line from the cross-run difference in the remainder it splits. No test of deictic cues ("now", "above") in a grading instruction was found, in LLM work or in survey question-wording research (nearest: Zhang, Meng and Collier 2024, arXiv 2406.17095, abstract only: models "do not have relative position awareness of the context"). Search: WebSearch and arXiv abs/HTML, 2026-11-05: LLM judge instruction wording sensitivity, prompt template grading score shift; closing or trailing instruction wording, self-evaluation of the model's own quoted response; self-critique prompt wording against a neutral instruction; deictic "above" wording, relative position in prompts; survey question wording and self-rating leniency; LLM judge run-to-run nondeterminism; self-preference framing, third-person lead-in; Chen et al. 2606.05976 v2 §4.4-4.5 and Tables 4 and 7 re-opened. By a fresh claude-opus-5-5 Novelty session (subagent).
